course_description: Introduction to the peoples and cultures of Early Medieval England (c450-c1100), with primary emphasis on texts written in Old English and Latin. Interdisciplinary approach including history, literature, religion, and material culture. Attention to literary genres ranging from elegy to riddles; the development of Christianity; encounters with Romans, Vikings, and Normans; and other political and social concerns. All readings in translation.
course_summary: Explore the history, literature, religion, art, and culture of early medieval English through texts in Latin and Old English. Covers Christianization and Viking encounters, concluding with the Norman Conquest. No prior experience with medieval literature is required.
learning_outcomes:
- Recognize and discuss major forms, techniques, and genres shaping English literature and culture.
- Discern and integrate divergent perspectives, question assumptions, and assess evidence related to Early Medieval England.
- Write compelling arguments that extend beyond summary to analysis and critical thinking.
what_you_will_learn:
- The history, literature, religion, art, and culture of early medieval English.
- How Early Medieval England was formed and Christianized.
- The influence of modern writers on Old English and Anglo-Latin literature.
